sections.h2: Where is Covington, Kentucky, and what shapes its housing?
sections.html:
Covington sits on the south bank of the Ohio River, directly across from Cincinnati, where the Licking River forms its eastern edge against Newport. It is the largest city in Northern Kentucky and the seat, with Independence, of Kenton County. The Census Bureau estimated 41,847 residents on July 1, 2025, on just 13.20 square miles of land, which works out to about 3,100 people per square mile in 2020. That density comes from a street grid of older rowhouses, cottages and mansions.

The city counts 19 neighborhoods, many of them within 12 historic districts concentrated in the northern part. Covington also annexed land to the south in recent decades, so the southern end has newer subdivisions.

sections.h2: How did Covington's history leave its mark on older houses?
sections.html:
Three men bought a 150-acre tract called The Point at the Ohio and Licking confluence in 1814 and laid out the town the next year, naming it for General Leonard Covington. It became a city in 1834. Tobacco, cigars, distilleries, glassworks and stove factories drew Catholic and German immigrants, and the Census Bureau placed the nation's center of population here for 1880.

By 1900 Covington was the second-largest city and industrial center in Kentucky, with almost 43,000 people. That boom period is why so many homes date from the late 1800s and early 1900s. Sellers of these houses should expect buyers to ask about plumbing, wiring and foundations, and about whether the property sits in a historic district.

sections.h2: Which Covington landmarks and neighborhoods do buyers recognize?
sections.html:
The John A. Roebling Suspension Bridge crosses the Ohio into Cincinnati and anchors the riverfront. MainStrasse Village, with its German-influenced blocks, is one of the best-known districts. The city has five churches on the National Register of Historic Places, among them St. Mary's Cathedral Basilica of the Assumption, built in 1895 and known for what is described as the world's largest handmade church stained glass window, and the German Mother of God church, finished in 1869. The Latonia neighborhood in the south has Holy Cross Church and School, built from 1906 to 1908.

Covington sits where the humid continental and humid subtropical climates meet, with hot, humid summers and cool winters. The mix means southern magnolias and blue spruce both grow in local yards, and a house here deals with freeze-thaw cycles and summer humidity alike.

sections.h2: What jobs support the Covington market?
sections.html:
Offices, health care and the airport. In the city's 2019 financial report the largest employers were the Internal Revenue Service (3,951, partly closed in 2019), Fidelity Investments (2,069), Club Chef (1,039), the Covington school board (914) and St. Elizabeth Hospital (408). The four-story OneNKY Center opened in September 2025 with a biotech lab and incubator, aimed at life sciences startups.

  • I-71, I-75 and US 25 serve downtown, and the Transit Authority of Northern Kentucky runs buses.
  • Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport, the state's busiest, is nearby and ranks among the top cargo airports in the country because of DHL.
  • Kenton County's website features the Brent Spence Bridge corridor project as a major long-term item.

sections.h2: How do Covington homes and incomes measure up?
sections.html:
Covington has a lower median home value than most of the Cincinnati area. Census Bureau figures for 2020 to 2024 put it at $187,300 for owner-occupied homes. About 51.8 percent of homes are owner-occupied, so rentals are common, and the median gross rent is $1,006.

  • Households: 18,265, averaging 2.21 people.
  • Median household income: $61,166. About 20.8 percent of residents live in poverty.
  • Median owner costs: $1,404 with a mortgage and $527 without.
  • Population change from the 2020 base to July 2025: up 2.2 percent.
  • Share of residents in the same home as a year before: 83.6 percent.

sections.h2: Which schools serve a Covington address?
sections.html: Most of the city belongs to Covington Independent Public Schools, the largest independent district in Kentucky. Its Holmes Junior/Senior High School is the oldest public high school in the state. The southern portions of the city fall in the Kenton County School District instead. Catholic options include Covington Latin School and Holy Cross High School, and Calvary Christian School is a Baptist school in the city. Give buyers the district for the address, since it affects the tax bill as well as enrollment.

sections.h2: What rental and short-term rental rules does Covington enforce?
sections.html:
Landlords here need an occupational license and a separate rental license. The city's January 2022 notice described fines of $250 for a first offense, $500 for a second and $750 for a third for operating without a license, and it said the city may order a property vacated if citations are ignored. At that time rental licenses ran from $30 for a one-unit parcel to $150 for 100-plus units, lasted three years and required an inspection.

  • Short-term rentals of 29 days or less need an annual license.
  • Under a June 2024 ordinance, the annual short-term license is $500, renewal is $250 and a reinspection is $100, with an $80 change-of-use fee.
  • Density caps total 151 non-host-occupied licenses citywide.
  • Code Enforcement enforces property maintenance, nuisance and zoning codes and does periodic on-site inspections. The city's 2022 notice gave (859) 292-2167 for questions.

If you are selling a rental, confirm the license is current before you list.

sections.h2: How do Kenton County taxes work for a Covington sale?
sections.html:
The Kenton County Sheriff bills and collects until the close of business April 15. Unpaid bills then go to the County Clerk, whose annual tax sale in July can pass a bill to a third-party buyer.

Kenton County Sheriff collection schedule
Payment windowAmount due
October 1 to November 1Face amount less 2%
November 2 to December 31Face amount
January 1 to January 31Face amount plus 5%
February 1 to April 15Face amount plus 10% plus 10%
  • Pay at 1840 Simon Kenton Way, Suite 1200, Covington, or at the Independence courthouse, 5272 Madison Pike.
  • Mail checks to Kenton County Sheriff, P.O. Box 188070, Erlanger, KY 41018.
  • No bill by October 15? Call the Sheriff's Office at 859-392-1800.
  • A $50 fee applies to returned checks.

Per the sheriff's FAQ, a seller pays their portion to the buyer or the buyer's escrow company at closing, and the owner of record then owes the whole bill. Take the same approach in your contract.

sections.h2: Can I appeal a Covington valuation in Kenton County?
sections.html: Yes, and the county PVA lays out the path. Call 859-392-1750 or file a Review Request with burden-of-proof documents such as comparable sales, appraisals, repair estimates and photos. The conference may be handled by email or in person by appointment, and it may start any time after January 1 and must finish before the roll's open inspection ends. For 2026, conferences closed May 18 at 4:15 pm and appeals to the clerk were due May 20 at 4 pm, both already past. Later appeals go to the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals. The PVA office is at 1840 Simon Kenton Way, Suite 3300, and also lists a homestead and disability exemption form.

faqs.q: What is the latest population figure for Covington, KY?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimated 41,847 people on July 1, 2025, up 2.2 percent from the 2020 estimates base.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Covington?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau reports $187,300 for owner-occupied homes from 2020 to 2024, with a 51.8 percent owner-occupied rate.

faqs.q: Do Covington landlords need a rental license?
faqs.a: Yes. The city requires an occupational license and a separate rental license, and unlicensed operators have been cited with fines starting at $250.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax for a Covington house?
faqs.a: The Kenton County Sheriff, through April 15. After that date unpaid bills move to the Kenton County Clerk.
Covington Independent Public Schools serves most of the city, and the Kenton County School District covers the southern portions.
